articles.title: Kimi Antonelli: How Formula 1's newest world champion has rewritten the record books at barely 20 years of age
articles.summary: Explaining the significance Kimi Antonelli's world championship triumph carries when placed in historical context; see the records the young Mercedes driver has broken during his first two seasons in Formula 1
articles.body:
The Italian youngster has reached the summit of motorsport in just his second season at the top level after a stellar campaign in which he has won nine races for Mercedes.

And while a world championship triumph for any driver is notable, Antonelli's first title carries particularly strong historical significance.

Beating Vettel's 16-year youngest benchmark

Formula 1 has a new youngest world champion in the sport's 76-year history.

After holding the record for 16 years, Sebastian Vettel spell as F1's youngest-ever champion has been beaten - by a full three years.

Vettel was aged 23 years and 134 days when he won the first of his four world titles with Red Bull in 2010. Antonelli clinched his maiden crown aged 20 years and 68 days, a record that may well stand for decades - if not, all time.

Antonelli also follows Jacques Villeneuve (1997) and Lewis Hamilton (2008) in winning his first F1 title in just his second season competing at motorsport's top level.

Ending Italy's seven-decade wait for another champion

Antonelli has also made history as an Italian driver in F1.

Considering an Italian won three of the first four Drivers' Championships following F1's inception in 1950, and Ferrari is the sport's most successful team, there had been a dearth of individual success in recent decades before Antonelli came along.

Antonelli is Italy's first world champion since 1953, when Alberto Ascari clinched his second and final title.

Antonelli's nine wins this year have already put him second to Ascari (13) in the list of Italian race winners.

One of those wins came on home soil, at Monza in September, which made Antonelli the first Italian winner of the Italian Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966.

While Max Verstappen's win as an 18-year-old at the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix remains the youngest for a driver in F1, Antonelli is the only driver to win multiple races as a teenager.

He won six races before his 20th birthday in August.

He did become the sport's youngest polesitter (China) and the youngest to lead the world championship (Japan) this year, along with the youngest to claim a pole-win-fastest lap hat-trick (China). He is also the youngest to achieve a Grand Slam - which requires a driver to add the lead of every race lap to a hat-trick - in Monaco.

In addition, he became the first driver to win his first five races in succession thanks to an unbeaten run from China to Monaco.

He was already the youngest driver to lead a race and claim a fastest race lap, feats he achieved as an 18-year-old in 2025.

Hendrick Motorsports drivers had quite the afternoon at Martinsville Speedway.

William Byron dominated the Xfinity 500 to pick up his first win of the season.

Kyle Larson kept his significant advantage in the NASCAR Cup Series points standings to feel comfortable about winning the championship next weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway.

Larson needs to earn just nine points from the race to become the 2026 Cup Series champion.

The No. 5 car drive owns a sizable advantage over Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin.

Bell and Hamlin need to have perfect races next week at Homestead-Miami and have Larson end up with one of the worst finishes of his career.

There's a high likelihood that Larson could clinch the title prior to the end of the race due to the points attached to the top-10 finishing places in each of the two stages.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari need to have 'serious talks' after Charles Leclerc
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari need "some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers in Mexico.
articles.body:
Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari "have to have some serious talks behind closed doors" after fighting between their two drivers cost them victory in the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Leclerc cut a chicane on the first lap to take the lead from Hamilton, who then lost second place to Max Verstappen as a consequence of his team-mate's attack.

Verstappen went on to win the race with Hamilton second as Kimi Antonelli finished third to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history.

"Ultimately, that lost us the win today," said Hamilton. "We have to have some serious talks behind closed doors."

During a red-flag period in the race caused by a crash for Valtteri Bottas' Cadillac, Hamilton had said over team radio: "We've got big problems. Big, big problems."

When informed Hamilton was unhappy, Leclerc said: "I will speak with Lewis. We both didn't make the corner. I don't know if Lewis' point was for me to get P3 but having the Red Bull second I felt it was worth it to keep the position and see what happened. That's what I did.

"I could be also unhappy with how much he pushed me off track out of Turn One, but it is racing. When you are fighting for a win it is the way it should be."

Hamilton's point is that if the Ferraris had worked together on the first lap, they would have been running one-two and could have controlled the race from there and likely finished in those positions.

The incident was the latest and arguably most serious of a series of tensions between Hamilton and Leclerc this season.

It follows Leclerc pushing Hamilton off track at the first corner of the Italian Grand Prix.

The race before that, Leclerc ignored a team order to let Hamilton by when they were on different strategies.

In Singapore last month, there was another incident when Hamilton felt he should have been let by when they were on different tyres, but Ferrari refused to make the call.

Verstappen, who capitalised on this latest battle in Mexico, said: "Ferrari were really fast, I do think they made it a little bit difficult for themselves fighting each other and that's why I was able to capitalise on that. I mean, I take it, right?

articles.body: Aston Martin vivió un infierno en la Ciudad de México. Lo que podía ser el mejor fin de semana de la temporada 2026 con unos libres que colocaron al AMR26 a las puertas de la Q3, las dos sesiones de la verdad cambiaron el tono. A uno negativo y un ridículo más de Honda, la parte más débil del conjunto. Fernando Alonso sólo pudo dar una vuelta lanzada en la clasificación y en carrera no pasó de la vuelta 6. Su sexto abandono del año, con los 12 de Stroll -que cedió en el giro 7 en México- ya van 18. “El coche es muy bueno, pero no podemos dar más de un número de vueltas con el motor”, reconoció el asturiano. En esta ocasión, un problema similar al del sábado relacionado con la presión que se disparó en la altura de la Ciudad de México. Hay chasis, la degradación es positiva y el foco de problemas es el mismo. Con una unidad de potencia que es una colección de problemas. El piloto asturiano ya pensaba más en 2027 que en algún resultado en las cuatro carreras que restan en la presente campaña. “Espero que podamos aprender la lección y llegar mejor preparadas a la próxima temporada”, añadió. Una advertencia importante, aunque en Honda esperan que la mejora sea notable tanto al inicio como en la primera parte de la temporada siguiente. Quizá Brasil, en siete días, ofrezca alguna garantía más. “Lo intentaremos de nuevo, sí. Yo intento hacer todo lo mejor, cada día lo hago. Cada vuelta, cada mañana, cada preparación que hago y cada comida que pruebo”, enumeró. Algo que siempre ha repetido el 14, pero en la F1 la mecánica es vital para tener alguna opción. Y en 2026 no han existido con una de las peores temporadas de su carrera deportiva. Eso le hace ser realista. Repitiendo el dardo a una Honda que sigue decepcionando pese a que se espera realmente poco a estas alturas del 2026. “Todo lo enfoco en rendir lo mejor posible detrás del volante, pero no soy capaz de acumular suficientes vueltas”, cerró el bicampeón.

articles.title: Kyle Larson Is Just One Race Away From Another NASCAR Championship — Can Anyone Stop Him at Homestead?!
articles.summary: One race remains in the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season, and Kyle Larson is now just one weekend away from potentially securing another championship. After Sun...
articles.body:
One race remains in the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series season, and Kyle Larson is now just one weekend away from potentially securing another championship.

After Sunday's race at Martinsville Speedway, the championship picture is nearly settled. Larson survived a difficult afternoon, finishing ninth in the Xfinity 500, but still heads to Homestead-Miami Speedway with a massive 67-point lead over Christopher Bell.

Denny Hamlin sits third, 70 points behind Larson, while Chase Briscoe is fourth, 84 points back. Joey Logano rounds out the top five, trailing by 103 points.

That means Larson has a significant advantage heading into the season finale, but there is still a championship to be decided.

Christopher Bell and Denny Hamlin are the biggest names standing between Larson and another title. Bell has the closest points deficit, while Hamlin has the experience and history of competing for championships. Both will need an enormous performance at Homestead to make things interesting.

Larson had an opportunity to clinch the championship at Martinsville, but William Byron's victory and the results behind him kept the title from being decided early.

Homestead is a track that has delivered plenty of memorable championship battles over the years. NASCAR is returning to the facility for its season finale for the first time since 2019, bringing the championship fight back to a venue with plenty of history.

Larson also has a major advantage heading there. He won the most recent Cup Series race at Homestead in March 2025, giving him another reason to feel confident about the upcoming weekend.

But one bad day can change everything in NASCAR.

Bell and Hamlin will be looking to capitalize on any mistake, while Larson simply needs to put together a clean weekend and avoid giving his competitors an opportunity to close the gap.

After 35 races, everything comes down to one final Sunday.

articles.title: Should NASCAR Step In After Carson Hocevar’s Controversial Brake Checks End Austin Cindric’s Day at Martinsville?
articles.summary: ASCAR has a serious decision to make after Sunday’s race at Martinsville Speedway, and Carson Hocevar could find himself facing consequences. The Spire Motor...
articles.body:
ASCAR has a serious decision to make after Sunday's race at Martinsville Speedway, and Carson Hocevar could find himself facing consequences.

The Spire Motorsports driver became the center of controversy during the Xfinity 500 after appearing to brake-check Austin Cindric multiple times, ultimately causing significant damage to the No. 2 Ford and ending Cindric's race early.

The incident unfolded during Stage 2 after Hocevar spun on his own and reported over the radio that his car was undriveable. On the following restart, Hocevar appeared to slow abruptly in front of Cindric on the frontstretch, then did it again exiting Turn 2.

A third brake check proved to be too much for Cindric, who made contact with the back of Hocevar's Chevrolet. The damage was severe enough that the No. 2 team had to remove the hood while attempting repairs before eventually taking the car to the garage.

Cindric made his frustration clear over the team radio.

"NASCAR, what are we doing? Like, we're just weaponizing cars here. I stack on entry with the guy and he has a mental breakdown."

And he wasn't the only one questioning Hocevar's actions. Other teams also expressed frustration over the radio, with Christopher Bell's crew chief Adam Stevens and Austin Dillon both questioning whether Hocevar's earlier spin was intentional.

This situation raises an even bigger question about NASCAR's responsibility to police aggressive driving.

Hocevar has developed a reputation for being one of the most aggressive drivers in the Cup Series. He has been involved in several controversial incidents over the past few seasons, including confrontations with Ryan Blaney and Austin Cindric.

NASCAR has previously handed Hocevar penalties for on-track incidents, including a $50,000 fine and a 25-point deduction in 2024 after an incident with Harrison Burton.

But should repeated brake checks that put another driver's equipment and safety at risk result in a more serious punishment?

There is a difference between hard racing and deliberately slowing down in front of another competitor. Drivers are expected to race aggressively, but using a race car to retaliate can create dangerous situations for everyone involved.

The timing makes this even more interesting. Martinsville was the final race before the championship finale at Homestead, and Cindric was left with a damaged car and a disappointing result.

NASCAR now has an opportunity to review the footage and decide whether further action is necessary.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes F1 world champion: How Mercedes driver clinched title in Mexico
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli seems destined for Formula 1 greatness after winning his first world title, writes Andrew Benson.
articles.body:
Just after Kimi Antonelli clinched his first title to become the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history, Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen were united in their assessment of his achievement.

"Incredible," they both said. Coming from the two most successful champions on the current grid, the men who are first and third in the all-time list of F1 record-holders, it meant something.

That Antonelli shared the Mexico City Grand Prix podium with these two titans meant something, too.

To Antonelli, firstly, who said: "I will definitely frame the picture and put it in my house because it's just an incredible moment. And as well to see so much respect from two incredible drivers who have done the history of the sport is truly special and a moment that will live and will always be remembered."

So, too, though, for its symbolism. Antonelli seems destined to join them among the list of all-time greats of the sport, judging by the scale of his achievement this year.

"There are going to be others," said 1996 world champion Damon Hill, commentating for BBC Radio 5 live.

"I don't see anything else other than him getting better and better. He's going to have to go through hard times as well, but no one is going to doubt his incredible talent."

Antonelli - the boy 'born in a garage' who became world champion

Antonelli heads list of F1's youngest champions

How much do you know about F1 champion Antonelli?

Antonelli's first title comes at the end of only his second season in F1. When he was drafted into Mercedes last year - to replace Hamilton, no less - there were those who said he was too inexperienced.

For some of last year, he looked it. There were flashes of promise, but by and large it was a shaky debut season, one that did not live up to Antonelli's billing as potentially the next generational talent.

So when it became clear that Mercedes would start this season with the best car, it was his team-mate George Russell, who had comfortably beaten him in 2025, who was favourite for the championship.

But that was without reckoning on the remarkable step forward Antonelli made in his development over last winter.

He finished the first race on Russell's tail. He took his maiden victory in the second, the first of five consecutive wins with which he took control of the championship. Since then, he has never looked like losing it.

Even when Mercedes' early season advantage was wiped out by their rivals, Antonelli was always there, always a factor. Which is more than can be said for Russell.

In that sense, it is important to see his achievement in context. Had the comparative performance between Russell and Antonelli carried on as it did last year, this championship may well have had a different complexion.

It could have been a season during which Russell and Hamilton were neck and neck in the title fight for most of the year - indeed, Russell has now slipped behind both Verstappen and Hamilton in the points table.

Instead, it has been a story of one driver's domination. His performances have been so strong that he has removed pretty much all jeopardy from the title fight.

That has not made it the most exciting season to watch, but it speaks volumes for the level at which Antonelli has performed. All because of the progress he has made - and his remarkable consistency.

"At his age," said Verstappen, "to be so solid, not make big mistakes, and of course also beat your experienced team-mate, he's just driven incredible, and I'm very proud of him, how he has handled himself this whole season."

Lando Norris, the outgoing world champion, was also effusive in his praise.

"It couldn't have gone to a better person," he said. "He's a genuine guy, very, very kind, and he has driven unbelievably well this year, better that what everyone was expecting of him.

"He's certainly not had an easy season in terms of his competition being incredibly high. He has gone up against the best drivers in the world, all in very good cars, and he's blown everyone away.

"I hope everyone gives him enough credit for what he's achieved this year. He's made everyone else look silly. He's driven that well and he's been able to click with his car, he's worked hard to understand how to drive this car and he's exploited it better than anyone else.

"So he should be very proud. He has achieved history and I am very, very happy for him."

For Antonelli, the difficulties of last year were formative, and critical in what he has been able to achieve this.

"The fact that some people said that I wasn't belonging to F1," he said, "or I wasn't ready for it - which at some point last year I probably looked like I wasn't - being able to experience those moments made me much more ready ahead of this year.

"Experiencing really low and difficult situations, high-pressure moments, really helped me to face certain situations this year and definitely they made me mature a lot as a driver, as a person.

"Still this year I've had moments where I could have done better, a lot better, so it's just a constant learning process.

"Last year being able to race straight into Mercedes, obviously straight under the spotlight, made me grow much faster than if I would have gone to a smaller team, for example."

He admitted after qualifying that he had been "tight", not driving as well as he could have, a result of the pressure of the moment.

"Austin, I was much more aggressive, much more present in the moment," said Antonelli, "while in Mexico, yesterday in qualifying, I was a bit more tense in a way because I also wasn't as intense in the way I was driving.

"So definitely, it hasn't been easy on that side. But now finally, we clinched it and now we can just enjoy the rest of the season."

The potency of the moment was clear to see after the race.

Antonelli admitted he was so emotional on the last lap as he followed Verstappen and Hamilton home that he was struggling to see.

"I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying basically and I couldn't see clearly ahead," he said. "I could see two Ferraris somehow with the tears.

"It was very special and a lot of memories went through my mind in that moment."

Then his father Marco and mother Veronica, who have been so important in his rise to F1, were there to greet him at the end.

Marco has been virtually ever-present this season, providing quiet support for his son whenever needed.

"To have my dad during the whole season was very important," said Antonelli, "because, first of all, he was the one keeping me grounded, especially after very high moments, but as well he was the one that was always there when I was facing a difficult situation or I wasn't feeling the best ahead of a session."

Then, in the champions' news conference, he became so emotional at one point as he remembered his late grandfather that he could not talk, and had to take a minute to compose himself.

"Oh my god," he said, after he had collected himself. "I cried way too much today. But it's good."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes F1 world champion: Mercedes driver says he couldn't see through his tears on final lap of Mexico City GP
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli has revealed he was overcome with emotion during the closing stages of the Mexico City Grand Prix, which he finished third in to seal the 2026 F1 Drivers' Championship; watch every session of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix from this Friday, live on Sky Sports F1
articles.body:
Antonelli finished third behind race-winner Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton to lower Sebastian Vettel's record of being F1's youngest world champion by over three years, sealing the title at 20 years and 68 days old.

The Italian was overcome with emotion on team radio and in several post-race interviews, and revealed he was already crying during the closing stages of the race.

"Already the lap before, I think I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically. I couldn't see clearly ahead," said Antonelli.

"I could see two Ferraris somehow with the tears. So, it was very special. A lot of memories went through my mind in that moment, all the memories since karting all the way to here.

"It was a very special final lap, and definitely, when I crossed the line, I let it all out because it was just achieving one of my biggest dreams. It was very special."

Antonelli is just the third Italian driver to win the F1 Drivers' Championship and the first since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

The Mercedes driver was lifted up by Verstappen and Hamilton on the podium with iconic Italian songs 'Nessun Dorma' and 'Sarà, perché ti amo' playing in the background, which Antonelli later revealed made him think about his late grandfather.

"The first song was very emotional for me because it was a song that my grandfather used to listen to always, so it was very special to hear that. I think he would be very proud," said Antonelli as he took a moment to compose himself through the tears in the post-race press conference.

"Oh my God, I've cried way too much today, but it's good. I just got very emotional because of my grandfather."

Antonelli: I will put podium picture with Verstappen-Hamilton in my house

It was somewhat fitting that Antonelli followed home two of F1's greatest drivers in Verstappen and Hamilton to become world champion.

Antonelli replaced Hamilton at Mercedes following the latter's shock move to Ferrari in 2025 and the 20-year-old says it was an "incredible" moment to share the podium with the two multiple world champions.

"It happened in Canada as well this year, earlier in the year, but obviously this is special. I will definitely frame the picture and put it in my house because it's just an incredible moment," he said.

"To see so much respect from two incredible drivers who have done the history of the sport is truly special, and a moment that will live and will always be remembered. So definitely I will frame the picture and put it on the wall of my house so I can see it very well whenever I go in."

Antonelli has been part of Mercedes since he was 12 years old and his father, Marco Antonelli, has been by his side at nearly every race since he made his F1 debut at the start of 2025.

Marco has a rallying team but flew into Mexico on Saturday morning with Kimi's sister to ensure they could watch Kimi become champion.

"It was a big effort for them to come here, and I'm very happy to be able to share and witness this moment altogether because my family has made, and they still do, an incredible amount of sacrifices for me," said Antonelli.

"Especially my dad, he has come to basically all the races this year, despite being very busy with his own work, his own job. So, you know, that has been crucial, to have such a figure.

"He was the one keeping me grounded, especially after very high moments, but as well he was the one that was always there when I was facing a difficult situation, or I wasn't feeling the best ahead of a session or ahead of the race.

"Then, of course, Mercedes, I couldn't thank them enough because, first of all, they were the ones who took the gamble when I was 11, and they were the ones who believed in me all the way, and they still do.

"t's been a massive privilege to be able to, first of all, race for this team. Hopefully we'll have much more success in the upcoming years.

"But as well, it's been a big privilege to work with Bono (Antonelli's race engineer Peter Bonnington) and with all the other guys, all the other boys and girls who always come to the track and do their best, because it's an incredible group, a very unique one and a very united one. And every single one of them has played a massive role in achieving this."

articles.title: George Russell: Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says British driver was 'distraught' after watching team-mate Kimi Antonelli seal 2026 F1 title
articles.summary: George Russell finished sixth in the Mexico City GP as his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli sealed the Drivers' Championship; Mercedes were fined after excusing Russell from carrying out his post-race media duties; Toto Wolff says Russell was "distraught" after the "catastrophic moment"
articles.body:
Russell began the season as the clear title favourite but has been comprehensively outperformed by Antonelli, who finished third in Sunday's race to become Formula 1's youngest ever world champion at the age of 20, with four rounds still remaining.

Russell started second on the grid, but a poor getaway - caused by a technical issue out of his control - saw him drop back to sixth on the opening lap, during which he was adjudged to have caused a collision with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar that would earn him a 10-second time penalty.

Before avoiding his obligatory media duties and leaving the circuit, Russell was one of the first to congratulate Antonelli in person as he embraced the Italian, after eventually finishing sixth himself.

Mercedes initially announced Russell wouldn't be doing any post-race interviews without providing a reason, but Wolff later explained the situation.

"I saw George after the race on the FIA scales, and obviously he's distraught about the situation," Wolff said.

"It was a great show of sportsmanship to go and see Kimi.

"I have known George for such a long time. So, I saw him and thought, for a racing driver, this is a catastrophic moment.

"And maybe today the race was a little bit a picture of his season. This was a race for him to win. We had the pace in the car. And we let him down on the first straight. The energy delivery is not what we thought it should be.

"And so I'm very much with him at the moment. I've been in situations where it's very, very difficult to cope.

"So, him not doing the media work, or leaving the track, is absolutely understandable. Him staying would have actually surprised me."

Mercedes were fined €5,000 by the FIA for Russell's absence from his media duties.

The result also saw Russell drop from second to fourth in the drivers' standings, with race winner Max Verstappen climbing two places and second-placed finisher Lewis Hamilton moving ahead of Russell but remaining third.

Russell is scheduled to speak to the media on Thursday in Brazil ahead of the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

articles.title: Mexico City Grand Prix driver ratings: How Max Verstappen and others performed
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Max Verstappen claimed his sixth Mexico City Grand Prix victory as Kimi Antonelli became the youngest world champion in Formula 1 history.

Verstappen held off Lewis Hamilton after a late safety car restart, while third place was enough for Antonelli to secure the title with four grands prix remaining.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Mexico City.

How Antonelli 'blew everyone away' to make Formula 1 history

'We've got big problems' - Hamilton says Ferrari need 'serious talks'

Antonelli becomes world champion as Verstappen wins in Mexico

Not quite a perfect weekend but a superb Sunday. Started fifth after a grid penalty and took full advantage of the Ferrari squabble ahead before holding off Hamilton through two restarts to claim his third win in four races.

A brilliant first Ferrari pole and arguably his strongest weekend with the team. Played his part in both drivers going too deep at Turn Four on lap one, but recovered to push Verstappen all the way and also set the fastest lap.

The pressure was enormous and he handled it superbly. Managed an excellent first stint on the soft tyre, produced a decisive move on Leclerc after the red flag and finished on the podium to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion.

There was plenty of speed after topping Friday practice and qualifying third, but Sunday's mistakes were costly. His off-track pass earned a penalty and the huge lock-up after the red flag dropped him off the podium when Ferrari had the pace to fight for victory.

Very quick at times, including topping final practice and Q2, but sixth on the grid left him with too much to do. His race pace was excellent and he finished right on Leclerc's gearbox, although losing places on the opening lap hurt his chances.

Missing pole by just 0.009 seconds was excellent and the lack of deployment at the start wasn't his fault. But spinning Isack Hadjar and picking up a 10-second penalty was a significant mistake on a day when much more was available.

An excellent recovery from the pit lane after his qualifying disqualification for a technical breach. Had already shown top-10 pace on Saturday and fought all the way through to seventh after penalties were applied.

Didn't have the outright pace of Nico Hulkenberg in qualifying but kept himself in contention during a chaotic race. Stayed clean when several around him didn't and was ultimately rewarded with eighth.

Another strong weekend that deserved more. Qualified seventh and had his race badly compromised when Russell spun him on lap one, so recovering to ninth after penalties were applied was decent.

An extremely impressive Formula 1 debut at very short notice. Started 18th, kept his head through all the interruptions and passed both Williams drivers late on before post-race penalties promoted him into the points.

Williams was again fighting towards the back but Albon at least led the team's challenge. Eleventh in the final order was his best result for 13 races, although much of that came through penalties elsewhere.

Another frustrating weekend in a difficult run of form. Finished behind Albon and was unable to turn a relatively chaotic race into the sort of opportunity Williams desperately needed.

There was some good recovery work after the shock Q2 exit and he fought his way to seventh on the road. But the collision that ended Arvid Lindblad's race was judged to be avoidable and the resulting 10-second penalty caps a weekend with too many errors.

Reaching Q3 was a good start to the weekend and he was firmly in the fight for points. Running into the back of Oliver Bearman after the restart undid that work and earned him a 10-second penalty.

A much better performance than the 15th looks on paper. Ran eighth on the road after a well-executed race, but failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags cost him 10 seconds and the points he had earned.

A spirited home race on his 300th Grand Prix start. Made up six places on the opening lap and ran as high as 13th before a slow pit stop and other issues knocked him backwards.

Qualifying ninth was excellent and he crossed the line in the points despite suffering power issues during the race. But failing to slow for double-waved yellow flags is a serious mistake and the resulting 30-second penalty dropped him to 17th.

A very strong weekend despite the DNF. Qualified eighth, raced confidently in the points and had just got ahead of Piastri before the McLaren driver was judged responsible for the collision that sent him into the barriers.

A solid recovery after qualifying 14th and he looked capable of fighting for points after passing Bortoleto. His retirement was through no fault of his own after Hulkenberg hit him at the restart.

Started at the back because of power-unit penalties and had made up ground before his frightening accident. The crash was caused by a car failure rather than driver error, so there is little reason for the DNF itself to hurt his score.

Qualified on the back row and barely had a race to judge. A battery-related problem forced Aston Martin to retire the car after only five laps.

Another weekend ruined by reliability. The MGU-K problem compromised qualifying and then reappeared almost immediately in the race, forcing him out after five laps.

articles.title: ¿Cuanto dinero se lleva Kimi Antonelli por ser campeón del mundo de F1?
articles.standfirst: Es el ganador más barato desde Nico Rosberg (2016) y menos que Norris en 2025
articles.summary: Es el ganador más barato desde Nico Rosberg (2016) y menos que Norris en 2025
articles.body: Una de las cuestiones que más curiosidad despierta cada final de año es cuánto ingresa el campeón del mundo en un deporte multimillonario como la F1. En el caso de Kimi Antonelli, debido a su sueldo relativamente bajo en el ránking por ser su primer contrato de novato en Mercedes, se ve penalizado en sus ganancias totales al final de 2026. Se estima en la mayoría de listas que está en dos o tres millones, pero parece que al ser su segundo año, su salario base está en cinco millones para este curso, según ha podido saber MARCA. Comparados con los 65 de Verstappen, los 60 de Hamilton o los 38 que se llevará Alonso en 2027 tras su renovación por Aston Martin suena a broma, pero para ser segunda temporada en F1 no está nada mal. Eso sí, Antonelli se va a beneficiar de una prerrogativa especial que sí aplica Mercedes y que no se hace en casi todos los equipos. La marca de la estrella prevé un bonus tanto por el Mundial de constructores, como por el Mundial de pilotos y parece que está en torno a los 10 millones por cada corona. La suma total arroja unos 25 millones para Kimi, con 20 años, a unos cinco de los 30 que se llevó Lando Norris por su primer título en 2025. Lo curioso es que George Russell, con su sueldo base de 15 millones anuales, se llevará una cantidad muy similar a la del joven astro italiano. Entre los dos no llegan a los 65 de Max y eso debe ser un motivo de alegría para Toto Wolff. Hay que recordar que los sueldos de los pilotos no entran dentro de los 205 millones de euros de límite presupuestario que se estableció para 2026 por la FIA. Eso sí, según parece su contrato inicial acaba al final de 2026 y le queda una reunión pendiente con Toto Wolff... y con Susie Wolff, que es quien le representa a través de 'management' de la que es directiva. No es muy difícil de imaginar que el nuevo sueldo de Antonelli puede superar los 30 millones, por lo que si es campeón en 2027 ya no será tan barato para Mercedes.

articles.title: Marc Márquez, un Mundial por bandera
articles.standfirst: Estas son las cuentas para ser campeón ya en Qatar
articles.summary: Estas son las cuentas para ser campeón ya en Qatar
articles.body: Llevar algo por bandera significa, popularmente, que una persona practica con orgullo algo, que lo realiza y muestra a los demás como un estandarte personal. Eso es lo que hizo Marc Márquez en Malasia, evidenciar que este Mundial de MotoGP es el del ilerdense, que en cuanto se ha convertido en una meta para él, no ha cejado en su empeño de hacerlo suyo. “A veces, la vida te da momentos especiales, momentos únicos”, decía el de Cervera y Sepang 2026 será uno de ellos, pues en él ha sentenciado esta edición. “Este gran premio me ha dado la oportunidad de aumentar el liderato, es la ocasión, pero tienes que hacerlo. Así que estuve súper concentrado en lograr el máximo número de puntos posibles; nos llevamos 34, lo que es muy importante para el Mundial”, señalaba después de su séptima victoria dominical del año. Porque el ‘93’ ha sacado la raza de campeón cuando más lo necesitaba, en una segunda mitad de temporada sublime, sin fallos, y sacando tajada de los errores del resto, especialmente de los competidores de Aprilia. “Este fin de semana fui al ataque desde la primera vuelta del primer entrenamiento libre y esa fue la clave. Es momento de atacar; cuando lo digo, lo hago”, soltó. Y la situación de Martinator, que acabó con su ausencia, sólo incrementó sus ansias. “Estaba muy concentrado. Cuando vi que Jorge Martín se bajaba del fin de semana, era el momento de hacerlo... y lo hice”, añadió. Así, en el trazado malasio, el leridano desató su furia a lo grande: se puso al frente en la primera curva, resistió el intento de adelantamiento de su hermano Álex y se marchó imponiendo un ritmo que pocos pensaban que se podía soportar con unos neumáticos que se destrozaban, como comprobó Bezzecchi, su otro rival. ‘Bez’, como Acosta, antes, hasta se topó con un Álex que hizo de escudero... mirando por sus intereses, pues pertenece a Ducati, por si alguno lo olvida. “En Qatar, Marc tendrá que espabilarse él solito”, bromeaba el del Gresini, pues se operará de la bursitis en su hombro derecho, la que ha hecho que se infiltre “en el 90 por ciento de las carreras”, como desveló el ‘73’. La exhibición del mayor de los Márquez hace que tenga su primera ‘bola de partido’ en Qatar. Las cuentas aún no están del todo claras, pero hay cosas seguras: no podrá ser campeón el sábado, porque le tiene que endosar 30 puntos a Martín. Claro que Jorge es duda y si no va o se retira, como en Malasia, todo estaría muy cerca el domingo. Si Marc vence en el Sprint y Martinator no suma, el del Ducati oficial necesitaría ser primero o segundo en la carrera larga para atarlo. Entra en juego, levemente, Bezzecchi, al que tiene que meter ocho puntos. Por cierto que en 2025, el nueve veces campeón del mundo se llevó de Lusail... los 37 puntos. Esta campaña, en Hungría ya le metió 33 puntos a Martinator y en Malasia estos 34. El título está casi tan atado como la bandera de España con el crespón negro por las víctimas del accidente ferroviario lo está al palo.
